message.content:
**Answer**

Lion (*Panthera leo*) and zebra (*Equus quagga*) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders:

| Species | Family | Order |
|---------|--------|-------|
| Lion | Felidae | Carnivora |
| Zebra | Equidae | Perissodactyla |

The last common ancestor of these two species is therefore the last common ancestor of the orders **Carnivora** and **Perissodactyla**. This ancestor lived in the **Paleocene epoch** (roughly 70–80 million years ago) and was a small, insectivorous mammal that belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.

So, in short:

> **The common ancestor of lion and zebra is a small, insectivorous mammal from the Paleocene that gave rise to the Laurasiatherian clade, from which both the Carnivora (cats) and Perissodactyla (horses, zebras, etc.) evolved.**
